PullRequest.Title: chat: expand customization migration assessment telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Intent

Follow up on #333196 with telemetry that can answer whether customization migration is improving:

- Are customizations already in the target's native location?
- Are they working only through compatibility mapping?
- Are they unsupported?
- Which bounded original source and customization type do those counts come from?

The existing event only reported a migration category and total count, so it could not distinguish those states or show movement toward native locations.

## Change

`chat.customizationMigrationAssessment` now emits one aggregate row per target harness, customization type, and original source:

```ts
{
  target,
  customizationType,
  source,
  nativeCount,
  mappedCount,
  unsupportedCount
}
```

File customizations are classified from the existing prompt inventory and target source folders. MCP servers are classified from the existing support snapshot's delivery and compatibility data. Disabled and out-of-scope MCP servers are excluded.

The assessment remains private to `CustomizationMigrationService`, which owns the inventory and emits the telemetry while computing the existing migration hint. `IChatService` and the hint-provider contract are unchanged; `ChatService` only drops the superseded aggregate emission.

## Non-goals

- no migration action/result telemetry
- no per-customization events
- no customization names, paths, IDs, descriptions, or content
- no change to migration hint UX or migration candidate behavior

## Review guide

1. `customizationMigrationServiceImpl.ts`: classification and aggregation
2. `chatServiceImpl.ts` and `customizationMigrationService.ts`: removal of the superseded aggregate transport
3. focused tests: assessment buckets, MCP exclusions, and remote target normalization

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- scoped telemetry extraction for `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat`
- focused Chromium unit tests: 115 passing

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed test proves the new unconditional calls even when categories are disabled; repository implementations prove the filesystem operations, the explicit 2-second readiness bound, and that `sendRequest` awaits the collector before agent invocation. Exact disk latency and how often the experiment enables hints vary, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem operations and an agent-host session-state wait
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On each eligible chat request, the five unconditional inventories fan out across the default locations for agents, instructions, prompts, skills, and hooks; under `once`, this repeats on every turn when no migration hint is produced, and source-folder discovery can wait up to 2 seconds for the first agent-host snapshot.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked chat request dispatch and increased time to first response
Findings.PreviousBehavior: `computeMigrationHint` called `computeMigration` for each category, whose existing enablement guard returned before file discovery for disabled categories. With the default settings, only prompt-file discovery ran; if there were no prompt candidates, `getSourceFolders` received an empty collection and did not wait for agent-host customizations.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added `Promise.all` invokes `listPromptFiles` for all five customization types regardless of which migration categories are enabled, then derives source-folder target types from the entire inventory. This performs discovery solely for telemetry assessment and can call `provideSourceFolders` for otherwise-disabled agents/instructions/skills/hooks.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 224-228 add unconditional `listPromptFiles` calls for every prompt type, replacing the old enabled-gated `computeMigration` calls. The changed test at lines 951-957 explicitly updates the all-disabled case from zero requested types/folders to all five types plus agent/skill source folders.
Findings.Title: Keep disabled-category assessment off the request critical path
Findings.Impact: With migration hints enabled by the experiment and the default migration-category settings (prompt migration enabled, the other file migrations disabled), a user who has native agent/instruction/skill/hook customizations but no prompt migration candidate now pays all-category filesystem discovery and may wait up to 2 seconds for remote session state before their message is sent. In `always` mode this occurs every turn; in `once` mode it also repeats while no hint is returned.
Findings.Evidence: `PromptsService.listPromptFiles` cold misses call `PromptFilesLocator.listFilesWithSource`, which resolves each configured/default location via filesystem/search operations; the defaults span multiple agent, instruction, skill, and hook locations. `AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideSourceFolders` awaits `whenCustomizationsReady`, whose production implementation has a 2000 ms first-snapshot timeout. `ChatService.sendRequest` awaits this hint collector in the request-context `Promise.all` before invoking the agent, so these added operations delay request dispatch rather than running as background telemetry.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the full assessment telemetry, but collect/cache it outside chat request dispatch (for example once per target/inventory generation after the request is sent), or at minimum keep hint computation enablement-gated and schedule the disabled-category assessment separately with invalidation on customization changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold Agent Host chat send with migration hints enabled and only the default prompt migration category enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `ChatService.sendRequest` creates the visible request, then awaits hooks, instructions, and `computeMigrationHint` together before invoking the agent. The changed assessment therefore must complete before the message is dispatched.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/search configured and default prompt-file locations for agents, instructions, prompts, skills, and hooks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One user and one workspace discovery per requested type, expanding to each configured/default source location; the added disabled categories account for multiple agent, instruction, skill, and hook locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled migration categories returned before calling `listPromptFiles`; with default settings only prompt inventory was needed for the file hint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All discovery promises are awaited before agent invocation; parallelism limits elapsed time to the slowest branch but creates additional I/O and can extend request latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the first Agent Host session-state subscription snapshot used by `provideSourceFolders`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared readiness wait per session subscription, followed by one in-memory folder projection per distinct target type; timeout is 2000 ms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When enabled prompt migration had no prompt candidates, source-folder target types were empty and this wait was not reached; unrelated disabled-category files now make it reachable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first wait directly blocks request dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build and settle the MCP support snapshot, including configuration resolution and installed-server assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scope per eligible hint computation, grouped by session type and normalized roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old hint computation unconditionally computed the same MCP migration snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before request dispatch, but this placement and cardinality already existed before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one telemetry log call per non-empty customization type/source assessment bucket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by distinct type/source combinations, not by customization count; realistic inventories produce a handful of rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Telemetry emitted only positive migration-category totals, at most four rows when a hint existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous sanitization/common-property merging and IPC enqueue occur before the hint returns, but the IPC response/network upload is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Five prompt inventories across roughly twenty built-in agent/instruction/prompt/skill/hook locations, plus user-configured locations and discovered files; source-folder queries scale with the distinct mapped target types in that inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The five inventories and MCP support assessment launch concurrently. After they settle, distinct target source folders are queried sequentially; their first agent-host readiness wait is shared/memoized and later target queries are in-memory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold miss, each prompt type performs discovery. `listPromptFiles` caches its promise once that type's locator event exists and invalidates it on file/config/provider changes. Agent-host readiness is memoized per session-state subscription but the first wait is bounded at 2 seconds. MCP support scopes are refcounted and disposed after this one-shot consumer, as before the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed tests prove all five inventories and source-folder calls occur when categories are disabled, and production call paths prove the boundary work and request ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency depends on cache warmth and configured locations, and the hint setting defaults to never but can be enabled by experiment. A delayed Agent Host snapshot has a concrete 2-second upper bound.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity eager-work regression because telemetry assessment for disabled categories introduces filesystem fan-out and a newly reachable bounded IPC wait on the message-send critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Subsequent chat turns in `once` or `always` hint mode when all customizations are native/supported and no hint is returned
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every eligible turn calls the assessment before agent invocation. `once` suppresses later calls only after an actual hint is shown, so a no-hint assessment repeats; `always` intentionally assesses every turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh prompt inventories after any relevant invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Usually cache hits; after invalidation, five type inventories on the next turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only enabled categories requested inventories, so disabled-category invalidations did not affect hint latency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache hits are cheap, but any cold/invalidated type blocks that turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per distinct type/source bucket per turn; bounded and typically small.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No assessment telemetry was emitted when no migration hint existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only local preparation and enqueue are synchronous; transport completion is off the critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows with chat-turn count and with distinct inventory type/source buckets after file-level aggregation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory promises are concurrent; target source-folder projections are sequential; telemetry rows are synchronously dispatched one by one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm prompt inventories reuse cached promises until invalidated, and session-state readiness is already settled. Assessment arrays/maps and telemetry payloads are rebuilt each turn; there is no assessment-result coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repeated invocation and bounded event cardinality; lower magnitude concern for telemetry because transport is asynchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Turn count and number of non-empty source buckets vary. The telemetry fan-out alone is bounded and not severe enough for a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported eager-work issue for disabled inventories. The bounded per-row telemetry does not independently meet the reporting threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization management editor computes file or MCP migration plans directly
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor awaits the selected migration computation to render candidates or perform migration; it does not call the new full `collectMigrationAssessment` path unless requesting a hint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover category-specific prompt files and read/write MCP configuration during explicit migration actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped by migration category and target type; explicit MCP writes remain per migration plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inventory and MCP migration boundaries existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for rendering or executing the user-requested migration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: File plans scale with candidate count and target folder count. MCP counting scales linearly with the support snapshot's server count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `computeMigrations` still starts four category computations concurrently. Individual source-folder target types remain sequential inside each file category.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: File inventory behavior remains category-specific. MCP support uses the existing refcounted scope lifecycle; no new persistent cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed return wrapper adds only an in-memory assessment-count loop to direct MCP computation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: MCP server lists and customization collections are normally modest; no evidence of large production cardinality was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; added work is bounded linear CPU/allocation without a new boundary or hot-path amplification.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and every diff page. Reported one high-confidence critical-path eager-work regression caused by unconditional all-category inventory and source-folder assessment. Checked cold/warm discovery caches, request ordering, agent-host/MCP scopes, telemetry fan-out, direct migration operations, concurrency, and lifecycle; no additional independent performance finding or qualifying regression fix was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
